In January 2018, debut author Josh Farkas visited Medium.com to discuss his book Quitting, which he writes serves as a cautionary tale for those considering a career quit vehicle to found an online company.
According to Farkas, he and his team started incubating The Art of Quitting after growing fed up with their previous nine-to-five job in August three years ago.
They proposed a straightforward concept for a business focused on assisting individuals in learning how to quit their jobs. To launch the company, they produced several flyers and handed them out in the vicinity of their location to advertise their recently established business.
At the outset, they faced their initial business challenge in vetting their company name.
Farkas does not advise starting any business with your name due to potential market saturation alongside other reasons.
Establishing a well-known name or a prosperous business is not an easy feat. Not to mention that devising a unique name to proceed is equally challenging.
Farkas’ experience can identify potential name conflicts years ahead of when a business is finally established.
In reality, while The Art of Quitting is not one of its best titles, it has undergone multiple revisions. Farkas stated that the business idea was initially called Art of Quitting, yet they encountered issues related to trademarks.
They pivoted again when confronted by a cease and desist letter from a website called Dead Wild Flowers, which had an existing similar title. Rather than facing the issue of possibly receiving cease and desist letters later, they chose to use a different name altogether.
During this period, they also explored different names using tools such as Verified Domains and Domainr. After chatting with another entrepreneur, this resulted in advice to find names by examining the existing company’s acronyms.
Losing the “quitting,” Farkas said he immediately identified with their current company name
